library_preparation_preflight.summary: graphql-dgs 10.5.0 needs no extra setup. Its POM pulls in graphql-java 24.1, java-dataloader, spring-context and spring-web (runtime), jackson-module-kotlin, kotlin-reflect and the coroutines libraries. Those cover schema loading, @DgsComponent/@DgsQuery/@DgsData discovery, and DgsQueryExecutor-style flows through a plain Spring AnnotationConfigApplicationContext.
risks: The artifact does not include DGS's Spring Boot autoconfiguration (graphql-dgs-spring-boot-starter) or the spring-graphql integration. Tests should build the DgsComponentProvider/DgsSchemaProvider wiring by hand with a Spring application context, not rely on autoconfig.

Most dependencies are runtime-scoped in the POM. They still reach the test runtime classpath, but test code that compiles directly against Spring or Jackson types may need those APIs added explicitly if Gradle does not expose them at compile time.

This research was a POM check plus a look at existing tests under tests/src/com.netflix.graphql.dgs (only graphql-dgs-subscription-types exists). I did not run Gradle or Native Image, so final reachability still depends on the local verification.
